title: Decompose daemon-command-registry before the graph kinds cross the line cap
description:
Filed 2026-08-17 by architect-2cc07e26 on the human's instruction, split out of task-931f99e8a84348689f97820acf0482bb's DoD 5 so it can land NOW instead of waiting behind that task's blocked services.

WHY NOW. apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts is 346 physical lines at HEAD a42ae2f (`git show HEAD:apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts | wc -l`). Epic rail 5 targets <=250 per production source and hard-splits before 400. task-931f99e8 must add FIVE graph mutation kinds (graph.approve, graph.prepare_supersession, graph.release_preparation, graph.request_expansion, graph.supersede), each needing a family entry, a capability entry and a payload allow-list entry. That crosses 400. Doing the split inside 931f99e8 would force one worker to refactor and wire in the same task, mixing a pure refactor with a behavior change in one diff -- the hardest possible thing for QA to grade. This task depends on NOTHING in the Graph Beta chain and de-risks it by landing first.

MEASURED STRUCTURE at HEAD a42ae2f:
- :1-43   imports (33 lines, ~10 subsystems)
- :45-48  CAPABILITIES
- :50-71  four frozen family maps: BOOTSTRAP_FAMILY (:50), REVIEW_FAMILY (:58), SESSION_FAMILY (:63), WORK_FAMILY (:68)
- :78-100 `agentCapabilitiesFor` -- EXPORTED and imported elsewhere
- :102-126 PAYLOAD_KEYS
- :127-131 OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES -- EXPORTED and imported elsewhere
- :149-155 OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS
- :156-173 decisionOf, :175-182 refusal
- :184-202 DaemonCommandPortOptions / DaemonCommandPorts types
- :203-346 `createDaemonCommandPorts` -- 143 lines, the composition root

THE NATURAL SEAM is the vocabulary/mapping half: CAPABILITIES, the four family maps, PAYLOAD_KEYS, OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES, OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS and agentCapabilitiesFor are all static tables about WHICH kind maps to what. Extracting them into a sibling module is exactly the surface task-931f99e8 will extend, so the split pays off immediately. The dispatch plumbing (decisionOf, refusal) and the composition root can stay, or move together if the arithmetic demands -- resolve at planning time against real line counts, not against this description.

TWO IMPORT EDGES TO PRESERVE (measure them yourself before moving anything):
- `agentCapabilitiesFor` is imported by apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:6 and re-exported through apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts (whose comment at :30 says the agent wrapper has ALWAYS imported it from that module).
- `OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES` is imported by apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts:12.
Either keep both symbols re-exported from daemon-command-registry.ts so no consumer path changes, or update every importer. Do not leave one importer on a stale path.

THIS IS A PURE REFACTOR. No command kind is added, removed or re-mapped; no capability, family or payload allow-list value changes; no refusal code or layer changes. The entire value is that the diff is behavior-free and therefore cheap to verify -- and that is also the whole risk, because a silent mapping change inside a mechanical move is invisible to a green suite.

NOT in scope: registering graph kinds (that is task-931f99e8), new runtime kinds, changing capabilities or payload allow-lists, touching the HTTP adapter or Authenticator, or any behavior change whatsoever.
definitionOfDone: Every production file touched is at or under 250 physical lines after the split, verified by an explicit line count in the completion note, and daemon-command-registry.ts specifically has room for five more kinds plus their family/capability/payload entries without approaching 400.

The complete mapping content is provably unchanged: a test enumerates every wired command kind with its capability, family and payload allow-list and asserts the full set against values captured BEFORE the split, so a silently altered or dropped entry fails rather than passing as a move.

Both exported consumer edges still resolve: `agentCapabilitiesFor` and `OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES` are reachable on the same import paths their existing consumers use (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts and apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts), proven by grep plus a compiled probe, not by reading the code.
Any new .ts module has its one-line .js bridge and loads under plain Node from apps/daemon, so the split does not create a module invisible to the .js import graph.

The diff is behavior-free: no command kind added/removed/re-mapped, no capability/family/payload value changed, no refusal code or layer changed; the completion note states this explicitly and names the check that would have caught a violation.

A mutation drill that alters ONE payload allow-list entry in the extracted module makes the step-2 enumeration test go red for that entry, proving the test pins mapping content rather than merely counting kinds.
pnpm typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm test are exit 0, each printing a nonzero Test Files count line, with no test file deleted or skipped to accommodate the move.
taskRails: PURE REFACTOR. No behavior change of any kind: no command kind added, removed or re-mapped, no capability/family/payload value edited, no refusal code or layer touched. If the split appears to require a behavior change, stop and report blocked rather than bundling one.

Preserve every existing import path for agentCapabilitiesFor and OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES, or update every importer; never leave a consumer on a stale path. Verify a moved symbol at its ORIGIN, not only at its destination.
A new .ts module needs its one-line .js bridge in the same commit, or it is invisible to the .js import graph and to plain-Node loadability.

Land BEFORE task-931f99e8 wires the graph kinds; this task exists so that refactor and wiring are never in one diff. Use TDD for the enumeration guard, target <=250 lines per production source, and commit only explicit owned paths by pathspec.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Chose the vocabulary/mapping half as the extraction seam because it is precisely the surface task-931f99e8 must extend with five graph kinds -- so the split pays off immediately rather than being generic tidying. REJECTED: (a) extracting `createDaemonCommandPorts` instead -- it is the composition root, the thing most readers arrive at, and moving it leaves the registry as a file of tables with a misleading name; (b) splitting per command family (bootstrap/review/session/work) -- four modules of a dozen lines each, and adding a fifth family would then mean creating a file rather than adding a row, which fights the registry's documented property that a command is added by registering an entry; (c) doing this inside task-931f99e8 -- that mixes a pure refactor with a behavior change in one diff, which is the hardest possible thing for QA to grade and the reason this task exists separately; (d) updating every importer instead of re-exporting from the registry -- more files touched for no benefit; a behavior-free diff should be as small as it can be. Kept the port types beside `createDaemonCommandPorts` deliberately: a factory and its return types in separate files costs a reader a hop and buys nothing. Step 5 leaves a second split (the dispatch plumbing) as a conditional, decided against real line counts rather than guessed now.

Its header states the design property to preserve: "Everything command-specific lives here... The HTTP seam reads only the registry, so a command is added by registering an entry here rather than by editing the boundary or the composition root." CONSUMER PATHS, both live: `agentCapabilitiesFor` is defined here and RE-EXPORTED through daemon-store-dependencies.ts (comment at :30 explains the agent wrapper has always imported it from that module); the actual importers use the store-dependencies path -- orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:6 and daemon-command-registry.test.ts:12. `OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES` is imported from the registry directly by daemon-store-dependencies.ts:12 and by the test at :11. EXISTING TESTS: daemon-command-registry.test.ts already contains a table-driven capability test at :203-218 that iterates rows through `agentCapabilitiesFor`, asserts OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES equals [ADMIN, GOAL, PLANNING, REVIEW, WORK], and asserts it is frozen -- strengthen this rather than adding a parallel suite. daemon-command-registry-continuation.test.ts is a second suite over the same module and must stay green. A new .ts module in this repo needs a one-line .js bridge or it is invisible to the .js import graph and to plain-Node loadability.
planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk on a pure refactor is a silent mapping change inside a mechanical move -- a dropped payload key or a swapped capability -- which no green suite catches unless a guard pins the mapping CONTENT. Two failure modes make that guard useless and both are easy to write by accident: deriving the expected values from the production tables at runtime (the test then agrees with whatever the table holds), or capturing the baseline AFTER the move (the same tautology with extra steps). Step 1 takes the dump first and step 2 requires hand-transcribed literals; the step-6 drill proves the guard actually pins content. Second risk is the two consumer paths for `agentCapabilitiesFor` -- registry-direct and via daemon-store-dependencies: breaking the second is invisible to a registry-focused test run, so step 4 requires a compiled probe against BOTH paths. Third, verify the move at its ORIGIN, not only the destination: a symbol left defined in both files typechecks, passes, and drifts later. Fourth, frozen tables can silently unfreeze when moved through a spread -- the existing test only asserts `Object.isFrozen` on OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES, so check the family maps and PAYLOAD_KEYS too. Fifth, a type-only import can erase a runtime value that was previously present. Sixth, the new module needs its .js bridge in the same commit. Finally, this must land BEFORE task-931f99e8 -- that task adds five kinds plus their entries and would otherwise cross the 400 hard cap mid-task, forcing exactly the mixed refactor-plus-wiring diff this task exists to prevent.
